summary: All three blocking findings identify unresolved timeout lifecycle contracts and require bounded spec repairs.

items.title: Descendant termination has no concrete target
items.rationale: The no-descendant guarantee cannot be implemented or tested from direct-child signaling alone; the spec must identify a process-tree termination strategy and its platform behavior.
items.evidence: src/lib/agent.js currently calls child.kill on a normally spawned child, while R4 requires descendants to be absent after settlement.

items.title: Grace expiry is treated as terminal before death is observable
items.rationale: SIGKILL dispatch is not proof of process death, so timeout settlement must wait for an observable tree-dead and direct-child close condition within the bounded margin.
items.evidence: The current spec names grace expiry as a terminal race but separately requires no live process after the returned failure.

items.title: Close after timeout has no caller-visible error contract
items.rationale: Deadline ownership must decide the result of a close during grace; otherwise success, ordinary exit error, and AgentTimeoutError are all plausible incompatible outcomes.
items.evidence: R3 covers survival through SIGKILL and pre-deadline close, but does not define close after timeout has fired.
